small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the conv output POOL*POOL=4 times per output pixel (once per pool cell) — fuse the pool inside the conv loop so each conv position is computed exactly once and accumulated into the pool sum. This alone should yield ~4x.
- Increase BLOCK_HW to 128 and try BLOCK_OC=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2-3; autotune over {(32,128),(64,64),(64,128),(128,32)} with the IC-loop unrolled in chunks of 4 or 8.
- Hoist the bias load out of the (dh,dw) loops (currently reloaded POOL*POOL times) and replace the (exp(v)-exp(-v))/(exp(v)+exp(-v)) tanh with `2*tl.sigmoid(2*v)-1` which is cheaper and more numerically stable.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM conv: one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile). For each pooled output position, loop over the POOL×POOL cells inside the kernel, gather KH*KW*IC into the GEMM-K dimension via tl.dot, apply (-SUB1, tanh, -SUB2), then average into the pooled accumulator. This avoids the POOL² redundant conv recompute and uses tensor cores.
- Alternative: persistent kernel where each program owns a pooled tile and streams IC in chunks, using tl.dot on (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) × (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_HW*POOL*POOL) reshaped tiles. Keep weights in shared/registers across the POOL×POOL inner iterations.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) input layout so the IC reduction is the contiguous axis — coalesced loads and better tl.dot K-dimension tiling. Pre-transpose x and weight once at init/forward entry.
